_comment: Draft recaps, written from the fact pack that scripts/history/draft-recap.ts builds.
Committed rather than only stored in Postgres so they are reviewable in a diff and
survive a database rebuild — the same reason every other source here is a file.
Every figure in these paragraphs comes from that fact pack; run
to see exactly what was available, and --seed to load this file into the database.
Re-running without --seed regenerates them through the API and overwrites these.

recaps.2021: Denver was the year the room decided the game was running backs and nothing else: 51 cents of every dollar went to the position, four backs cleared $58, and Bryan's $66 on Christian McCaffrey set the mark. Jack got Ja'Marr Chase for $2 and watched him finish WR4 — then lost the final to Daniel, who put together the best draft in the room and converted it into the title. Bill's $38 on Calvin Ridley bought him WR50.
recaps.2022: Bryan paid $52 for Jonathan Taylor, the most expensive pick of the night, and got RB28 out of it; Jack's $32 on Javonte Williams came back RB42. Bolek spent to the dollar — all $200, topped by Austin Ekeler at $44 — and picked up Tyler Lockett for $1 on the way to WR16 and the title, beating Bill in the final. Justin took the regular season, and Nate drafted the best board of the ten.
recaps.2023: Daniel found Raheem Mostert for $1 and got RB2 out of him, which is roughly how you win a regular season and grade out as the best drafter in Nashville. It bought him neither trophy: Mario took the title with $194 spent and nothing pricier than $44 on Christian McCaffrey, beating Gabes in the final. Nate's $42 Nick Chubb finished RB45, and Eric/Blakey's $47 Justin Jefferson finished WR28.
recaps.2024: Justin spent two dollars in total on Brian Thomas and Jaxon Smith-Njigba and got back WR4 and WR7 — the best draft anyone has had in this room. Nate went about it differently, burning $169 of his $200 before pick 40 with nothing pricier than $37 on Derrick Henry, and won the whole thing; his victim in the final was Eric/Blakey, who had both the night's most expensive pick ($55 on Josh Allen) and the best regular season. Jack's $47 on Christian McCaffrey finished RB44.
recaps.2025: Bryan had $188 of his budget gone by pick 40, which is one way to attack a room. Gabes did the opposite — nothing over $35, CeeDee Lamb the priciest thing he owned — and won the title anyway, despite $27 on Malik Nabers turning into WR42. Jack took the regular season and lost the final, though his $3 on Travis Etienne came back RB10, and Mario quietly drafted the best board in Scottsdale.
